hypothesis: Aggregate latent energy can dilute abnormalities confined to a few coordinates. Test sparse departures and their concentration, retaining the same frozen normal density models and physical inference.
models: Three frozen R3 four-noise-view summary flows; R4 continuous per-map physical coordinates. No neural retraining.
inputs: The existing 72 physical summaries of each map. Extract all 72 Gaussianized latent coordinates at that map's frozen R4 energy-minimizing physical coordinates. Known true cosmology is used for NORMAL diagnostics only.
normal_fit: Per-seed coordinate means and standard deviations from the 3232 normal validation latents at inferred cosmology. No calibration/audit/proxy or public inputs fit these moments. Retain raw-energy/raw-maximum controls.
scores: Raw sum of squared coordinates, reproducing R4 continuous energy
Sum of squares after normal-validation coordinate standardization
Mean of the four largest standardized squared coordinates
One-sided Berk-Jones-style tail aggregation over the smallest 1..36 two-sided Gaussian tail values; numerical tails clipped to [1e-300,1-1e-12]
Angular concentration: 72 times largest standardized square divided by sum of standardized squares
ensemble: Compute each statistic per seed, then average its three scalar outputs. Examine standalone diagnostics and fixed equal-mean / maximum combinations with normal-scaled candidate 08; these are exploratory diagnostic comparisons. Normal calibration medians and q90-minus-median supply all scales.
checks: Sum of extracted raw squares reproduces recorded profile energies
Singleton, reversed and chunked inputs give identical latents
Compare learned-coordinate normal tails against a fixed seeded 72-dimensional Gaussian simulation as a numerical control
Report every prior synthetic family and normal parameter-dependent false positives, including regressions
Retain per-seed results; latent axes are not averaged across seeds
If a sparse statistic appears useful, check whether profiling that statistic separately over physical coordinates changes the conclusion
data: Existing normal validation/calibration/audit sets and prior synthetic probes. These maps/families are reused. R4 fresh-noise closure is also now a reused diagnostic, not a new blind test for R5.
public_test: Not read or used for model selection in this experiment. Candidates 04 through 09 stay frozen.
limitations: The flow coordinates need not be independent or exactly Gaussian, especially after estimating cosmology from the same map.
Named sparse-testing asymptotic optimality does not apply automatically to this learned representation.
Empirical normal calibration, not the Gaussian tail transform, defines final thresholds.
Synthetic performance and repeated diagnostic selection do not establish competition performance.
scope: Authorized erdos-3242 lab only, RAM-backed directories, no production or GCS changes.
